definition.def: When you conduct an activity or task, you organize it and carry it out.
examples: I decided to conduct an experiment. [VERB noun]
He said they were conducting a campaign against democrats across the country. [VERB noun]
The council conducted a survey of the uses to which farm buildings are put. [VERB noun]

definition.def: The conduct of a task or activity is the way in which it is organized and carried out.
examples: Also up for discussion will be the conduct of free and fair elections. [+ of]
There is emerging opposition to his conduct of foreign policy.

definition.def: If you conduct yourself in a particular way, you behave in that way.
examples: The way he conducts himself reflects on the party and will increase criticisms against him. [VERB pronoun-reflexive]
Most of them believe they conduct their private and public lives in accordance with Christian morality. [VERB noun]

definition.def: Someone's conduct is the way they behave in particular situations.
examples: For Europeans, the law is a statement of basic principles of civilised conduct.
He has trouble understanding that other people judge him by his conduct.

definition.def: When someone conducts an orchestra or choir, they stand in front of it and direct its performance.
examples: Dennis had recently begun a successful career conducting opera in Europe. [VERB noun]
The choral director will continue to conduct here and abroad. [VERB]
At the Curtis Institute he studied conducting with Fritz Reiner. [VERB-ing]

definition.def: If something conducts heat or electricity, it allows heat or electricity to pass through it or along it.
examples: Water conducts heat faster than air. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you conduct someone to a place, you go there with them. [formal]
examples: He asked if he might conduct us to the ball which was to bring the proceedings to an end. [VERB noun]
